summary: The seam-dump probe (scope decision 1, rebuilt cfg(test)-only under src/tessellation) classifies the torus.json seam miss DECISIVELY as mechanism (a): the same shared edge is sampled at DIFFERENT per-face parameter sets, created AFTER the shared per-edge discretization by a per-carrier stage, and the leftover seam chains interleave (no coincident twins exist for the face-local injections at any weld tolerance). It is NOT (b) evaluation asymmetry — canonical samples emitted by both faces are bitwise identical positions (the lift pushes the original shared-edge sample `pt`, never a carrier re-evaluation) — and NOT (c) (no face emits zero seam vertices). The injecting stage is NAMED: the ACC-1 accuracy grid wiring (`wire_grid_segment` -> `interval_endpoint_vertex` -> `resolve_vertex` in tessellation/triangulation.rs) inserts a fresh CDT vertex wherever an interior sampling-grid segment crosses a SOURCE trim segment, splitting the shared seam constraint at a parameter only that face's carrier grid chose. On torus.json the probe measures, per shared edge, face-A/face-B seam counts like 13v12 and 33v29, with the over-count exactly the grid-cut injections (face0/edge1: 11 canonical identity + 22 injected vs face1/edge1: 11 + 18). A bounded expression of the packet's fix was implemented and MEASURED: grid cuts landing on SegmentOrigin::Source trim segments now snap to the segment's nearest canonical boundary sample (a position that is a pure function of the shared edge's own sample ledger) instead of inserting a fresh vertex; cuts on synthetic segments are untouched and no weld call site was added. Result: torus.json seam injections drop to ZERO on every edge (all face seam sample sets = the canonical set), pre-weld boundary edges drop 352 -> 192 (the remainder is per-face index copies of identical canonical positions), and the required reading suite moves from 4 failing -> 1 failing: solid_is_closed/csolid_is_closed now close fixtures 0,1,2 (bottle Irregular -> Closed, punched-cube, torus-punched-cube) and special_cylinder + special_cylinder_csolid are Closed; the ONLY remaining failure is fixture 3 (sphere.json, condition Regular). The sphere residue is a SECOND, distinct injection site the grid-wiring contract cannot reach: the pole-cap faces still emit 9-56 lift-bisection samples per shared meridian (e.g. edge 4, canonical 7 samples: cap face 5 identity + 9 injected vs its band neighbour 5 + 0), i.e. per-carrier boundary-LIFT continuity samples inserted on source seams near the collapsed pole axis. Closing the sphere requires routing the per-face lift's bisection/continuity samples through the same (EdgeID, ordinal) ledger (or a shared pole-origin contract) — the structural restructure r1's recommended amendment (A) names. Since the required suite cannot be made green without it and the change to the instrumented lift is not a bounded in-scope edit in this packet's remaining budget, no production change is committed; the working tree carries only this RESULT (the probe and the experiment were reverted). Edge identity IS available to the legacy mesher (compressed edge index; EdgeID via shared curve Arc in the shell path), so the packet's stop condition on missing identity was not triggered.
notes: Anchors verified against the pristine tree: A1 (put_together_same_attrs fn defs in filters/optimizing.rs) = 2, A2 (resources/shape uses in tests/tessellation/triangulation.rs) = 1. Baseline reproduction matches the packet: cargo test -p truck-meshalgo --test tessellation (quick profile) -> 4 passed / 6 failed (solid_is_closed + csolid_is_closed fail at file 0 bottle = Irregular; special_cylinder + special_cylinder_csolid = Oriented; compare_occt_mesh/_csolid = environmental NotFound on the absent ../obj/by_occt.obj reference). The bounded EdgeID-contract experiment (grid-cut snap to canonical seam samples on Source segments) was verified by the same suite -> 6 passed / 4 failed, the failures being the two recorded compare_occt environmental tests and sphere.json (Regular) in solid_is_closed + csolid_is_closed; fixtures 0-2 close and special_cylinder closes. No planar regression was observed in the experiment (planar faces agree on canonical samples, so snapping an injection to the already-agreed canonical sample is a no-op there; cube/cube-in-cube remain Closed with unchanged triangle counts). The probe (src/tessellation seam_dump, cfg(test)-only) was reverted with the experiment so the committed tree is byte-identical to the packet branch tip except for PACKET.md/CONTEXT.md dispatch edits.
deviation_notes: Diagnosis (packet scope decision 1): seam-dump probe on torus.json, per shared compressed edge, per face: (canonical identity samples, injected samples). BEFORE: edges 0/2/5 clean (13v12, 13v13); edges 1/3/6/7 (the periodic/major arcs) carry per-face injections: face0 edge1 = 11+22, face1 edge1 = 11+18, face2 edge7 = 12+22, face3 edge7 = 11+18; pre-weld boundary edges 352. AFTER the bounded fix: injected_samples = 0 on every one of the 8 edges of both faces; pre-weld boundary edges 192. Classification: (a) parameterization/identity mismatch by per-carrier grid-cut injection, exactly the packet's predicted mechanism; (b) disproved (canonical twins are bitwise identical); (c) absent.

Stop-condition audit: neither packet stop condition fired. Case (b) (evaluation asymmetry between carriers on the shared curve's embedding) was disproved by direct bitwise comparison of canonical seam twins. Edge identity is present in the legacy mesher's inputs (CompressedShell edge index threaded to every face wire; Shell path shares the curve Arc so edge.id() keys one polyline per edge), so no SPEC_GAP for missing identity is warranted.

The fix direction (per-edge sample ledger, no welding, no density matching, planar-immune) was executed in its bounded ACC-1 expression and measurably closes every analytic seam produced by the accuracy grid wiring, including the packet's headline fixture torus.json and the r1-era bottle Irregular class. The residual that blocks the full suite is the sphere pole-cap class: per-carrier lift bisection inserts continuity samples on shared source meridians near the collapsed pole axis, and the two faces of a shared meridian bisect differently (cap 9+ vs band 0+ on edge 4). That injection site sits in the boundary lift (PolyBoundaryPiece::try_new periodic/ambiguous-step refinement), not in the grid wiring, and making it a pure function of the shared edge requires the per-face lift restructure of r1's amendment (A); it is not a bounded edit in the remaining budget and was not attempted beyond classification.

evidence.cargo_test_-p_truck-meshalgo_--test_tess: 4 passed, 6 failed (quick profile). solid_is_closed/csolid_is_closed: file no.0 bottle Irregular (first failing index); special_cylinder/special_cylinder_csolid: Oriented; compare_occt_mesh/_csolid: environmental NotFound.

6 passed, 4 failed. special_cylinder and special_cylinder_csolid Closed; solid_is_closed/csolid_is_closed reach file no.3 sphere = Regular (fixtures 0 bottle, 1 punched-cube, 2 torus-punched-cube now close); only the 2 recorded compare_occt environmental tests remain alongside sphere.
evidence.seam_dump_probe_torus_pre_fix: pre-weld boundary edges 352; per-edge face seam counts 13v12/33v29/13v13/33v29/13v12/13v13/33v30/34v29 for edges 0..7; injections present only on the periodic major arcs (face0 edge1: 11 identity + 22 injected; face1 edge1: 11+18; face2 edge7: 12+22; face3 edge7: 11+18). Canonical polyline = 13 points on every edge.
evidence.seam_dump_probe_torus_after_bounded_fix: pre-weld boundary edges 192; injected_samples = 0 on every face/edge pair; every face seam sample set is exactly the shared edge's canonical sample set.
evidence.seam_dump_probe_sphere_after_bounded_fix: 12 faces / 20 edges; pre-weld boundary edges 600; band faces clean (injected 0), pole-cap faces (2,5,8,11) still inject along shared meridians: e.g. face2 edge7 7 identity + 56 injected, face2 edge4 5+9, face5 edge7 6+34; edge 4 canonical polyline = 7 points.
evidence.mechanism_attribution: grid_segment_trim_intersections marks each grid/trim crossing of a SegmentOrigin::Source segment; interval_endpoint_vertex previously resolved such crossings with resolve_vertex, inserting a fresh CDT vertex on the shared seam at a face-local parameter. Snapping those cuts to the segment's nearest canonical boundary vertex removed every torus seam injection without touching synthetic/closure cuts or any weld call site (put_together_same_attrs sites unchanged at 2).

stop_conditions_checked.case_b_evaluation_asymmetry: NOT triggered. Canonical seam twins emitted by the two faces of a shared edge are bitwise identical positions (the lift carries the original shared-edge sample); injected vertices have no twin because they exist on one face only, not because equal parameters evaluate differently.
stop_conditions_checked.edge_identity_absent: NOT triggered. Compressed edges carry integer indices referenced by every face wire; the shell path shares the curve Arc so a per-edge polyline is built once per EdgeID. Identity is available and was used by the bounded fix.
stop_conditions_checked.suite_green_required_for_a_landed_fix: NOT reached. sphere.json remains Regular: its pole-cap seams are closed by per-carrier lift bisection samples, an injection site outside the grid-wiring contract that was bounded and verified here. A fix commit requires the sphere lift restructure (r1 amendment (A)); leaving the required reading suite red was rejected, so the experiment was reverted and nothing is committed.

recommended_amendment: Re-file a successor scoped to the boundary-LIFT injection site: in PolyBoundaryPiece::try_new, periodic/ambiguous-step bisection on a SegmentOrigin::Source piece must not emit per-carrier continuity samples onto the shared seam; the lift must consume the (EdgeID, ordinal) canonical sample ledger (already landed as EdgeSampleLedgerSet / triangulation_with_ledger, BG-CG-005) for source pieces and carry a shared pole-origin resolution for collapsed-axis seams (sphere caps), keeping grid-cut snapping from this run (it is correct, measured, and closes the r1 bottle/torus/special-cylinder class). Budget note: the ACC-1 grid-wiring expression of the seam contract is verified and ready to re-apply verbatim; the remaining work is the lift-side contract and its sphere-pole origin rule.
